question: What should detect frontier-model writing conventions in a draft of the owner's DM?

options.name: Today's AI-phrase index
options.description: Keep src/voice/aiTells as is: vale-ai-tells rules plus the Jina-embedded index of curated AI phrases, nearest chunk against the owner's p99.

options.name: Rule linter
options.description: Replace the index with a rule linter like eric-tramel/slop-guard (24 rules, 200+ heuristics) or renefichtmueller/slop-radar (600+ buzzwords, 16 structural patterns, TypeScript), muted where the owner uses the rule himself.

options.name: Owner-baseline over-use profile
options.description: The slop-forensics/Antislop method with the owner as the human baseline: words, bigrams and trigrams that agent drafts for his chats use far more than his own messages do, plus em dash, curly quotes and markdown habits; a draft is scored by the over-used n-grams it contains. Pure code, under 1 ms.

options.name: Small classifier on MiniLM
options.description: The Idiosyncrasies method: a logistic head on the shipped MiniLM embedding (and character n-grams) trained on his real messages versus frontier drafts written for his chats; about 6 ms on the CPU.

options.name: Perplexity zero-shot
options.description: Binoculars or Fast-DetectGPT with a small local causal language model (0.5-1.5B, ONNX on the CPU).

options.name: C + D + structure, length-calibrated
options.description: C and D combined with structural checks (opener repetition across the options, em dash and markdown leakage, sentence-length variance, Biber-lite features), calibrated per length band so 95% of his own messages pass in every band, abstaining on lines too short to tell; flags name the words beside how he says it; replaces the Jina index in the gate.

options.name: SlopTotal ensemble
options.description: Self-host pablocaeg/sloptotal: 23 detector engines with one calibrated score, on the CPU.

criteria.question: How reliably will the owner's own short casual messages pass (few false flags)?
How well will it catch frontier-model drafts written to sound like him?
Can it say which words or habit gave the draft away, beside how he says it?
How fast per option on this laptop's CPU, with no network?
How small is what it needs on disk and in memory?
How small is the build into log's voice score (TypeScript, onnxruntime, the MiniLM already shipped)?

question: Where should the frontier-model side of the training data come from?

options.name: Public AI-text corpora
options.description: Use public AI-vs-human datasets and curated AI phrase lists.

options.name: Drafts log already has
options.description: The agent drafts for his chats in log's run records and gate history, passed and failed.

options.name: Fresh drafts from several frontier models
options.description: For a few hundred of his real past moments (their message plus the chat), ask Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek to reply as him with today's grounding pack, and pair each with what he really said.

options.name: B plus C
options.description: Start from the drafts log already has, top up with fresh multi-model drafts on his real moments, refreshed when models change.

criteria.question: How close is it to the drafts the gate will actually see?
How well does it cover the different frontier models and new ones?
How cheap is it to make?
Does each AI example have his real reply to the same moment beside it?
